title: tte
description: Time to exhaustion at a power the CALLER names (#187). `status` is the honest qualifier: `in_model` (2-20 minutes, where the two-parameter model holds), `outside_model` (the number is real arithmetic but the model overshoots there — read it as a direction), or `below_cp` (at or under CP the model says indefinitely, which is the model's answer and not the athlete's). `known` here means only that the arithmetic ran — it is NOT the usual licence to trust the magnitude. WEIGH THE FIT BEFORE THE NUMBER, in this order: `fit_r2` is how well the line fits its own points and is the only quality signal that does not depend on what was asked (it is 1 by construction when `fit_points` is 2, where the count is the signal instead); `contradicts_model` is true when the longest effort at or above `watts` the athlete already has on record (`demonstrated_s`/`demonstrated_w`, from the same window the fit was built from) is LONGER than the prediction, meaning the model is refuted by its own inputs. `contradicts_model: false` is NOT evidence the fit is sound — it only fires where a recorded effort overlaps the queried power. `fit_points` is 3 for a perfect fit and 3 for a degenerate one. The fit covers `sport_family` over `window_days` and EXCLUDES its own anchor date — `tte` anchors on today, so a ride synced today is not in the fit that answers today's question. `activity.w_prime_balance` uses the same rule anchored on each session's own date, so the two differ by which date they anchor on and which family they cover, not by whether today counts.
